title: Inverse image of sheaves of sets along a composite of continuous maps
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ be continuous maps of topological spaces, and for a continuous map $h$ let $h^{-1}$ be the inverse image of sheaves of sets, left adjoint to the direct image $h_*$, with unit $\eta^h$ given on sections by $\eta^h_{\mathcal G,W}:\mathcal G(W)\to(h^{-1}\mathcal G)(h^{-1}W)$, as in [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] (2), (3) with values in sets. Then for every sheaf of sets $\mathcal G$ on $Z$ there is exactly one morphism of sheaves of sets $c_{\mathcal G}:f^{-1}g^{-1}\mathcal G\to(g\circ f)^{-1}\mathcal G$ on $X$ such that $c_{\mathcal G,(g\circ f)^{-1}W}\bigl(\eta^f_{g^{-1}\mathcal G,g^{-1}W}(\eta^g_{\mathcal G,W}(s))\bigr)=\eta^{g\circ f}_{\mathcal G,W}(s)$ for every open $W\subseteq Z$ and every $s\in\mathcal G(W)$; it is an isomorphism, and natural in $\mathcal G$.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma Tag 008I (label lemma-pullback-composition, line 2209): '(g o f)^{-1} and f^{-1} o g^{-1} are canonically isomorphic' (both left adjoint to (g o f)_* = g_* o f_*, Lemma lemma-pushforward-composition); the description by units is that of the isomorphism of left adjoints

proof.text: *Step 1 (direct images compose on the nose).* Write $\mathrm{Sh}(T)$ for the category of sheaves of sets on a space $T$. By [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] (1) (with values in sets), for a sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $X$ and an open $W\subseteq Z$ we have $(g_*f_*\mathcal F)(W)=(f_*\mathcal F)(g^{-1}W)=\mathcal F(f^{-1}(g^{-1}W))$ and $((g\circ f)_*\mathcal F)(W)=\mathcal F((g\circ f)^{-1}W)$, and $f^{-1}(g^{-1}W)=(g\circ f)^{-1}W$ as subsets of $X$. The restriction maps of both are restriction maps of $\mathcal F$ between the same opens, and for a morphism $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F'$ both $(g_*f_*\varphi)_W$ and $((g\circ f)_*\varphi)_W$ equal $\varphi_{(g\circ f)^{-1}W}$. Hence $g_*\circ f_*=(g\circ f)_*$ as functors $\mathrm{Sh}(X)\to\mathrm{Sh}(Z)$; call this functor $R$.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma Tag 008E (label lemma-pushforward-composition, line 2038) and its proof

proof.text: *Step 2 (the composite adjunction).* By [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] (3) (with values in sets) there are adjunctions $g^{-1}\dashv g_*$ between $\mathrm{Sh}(Z)$ and $\mathrm{Sh}(Y)$ with unit $\eta^g$, $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$ between $\mathrm{Sh}(Y)$ and $\mathrm{Sh}(X)$ with unit $\eta^f$, and $(g\circ f)^{-1}\dashv(g\circ f)_*=R$ with unit $\eta^{g\circ f}$. Apply [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] with $\mathcal A=\mathrm{Sh}(Z)$, $\mathcal B=\mathrm{Sh}(Y)$, $\mathcal C=\mathrm{Sh}(X)$, $F=g^{-1}$, $G=g_*$, $H=f^{-1}$, $I=f_*$: it gives an adjunction $L_1:=f^{-1}\circ g^{-1}\dashv g_*\circ f_*=R$ (Step 1) with unit $\eta_{1,\mathcal G}=g_*(\eta^f_{g^{-1}\mathcal G})\circ\eta^g_{\mathcal G}:\mathcal G\to R\,L_1\mathcal G$ and a counit $\varepsilon_1$ satisfying the triangle identities. Since $(g_*\psi)_W=\psi_{g^{-1}W}$ for a morphism $\psi$ of sheaves on $Y$ (definition of $g_*$), on sections over an open $W\subseteq Z$ this unit is $\eta_{1,\mathcal G,W}(s)=\eta^f_{g^{-1}\mathcal G,g^{-1}W}(\eta^g_{\mathcal G,W}(s))\in(f^{-1}g^{-1}\mathcal G)(f^{-1}g^{-1}W)$ for $s\in\mathcal G(W)$. Put $L_2=(g\circ f)^{-1}$ and $\eta_2=\eta^{g\circ f}$, also an adjunction $L_2\dashv R$.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma Tag 008I (label lemma-pullback-composition, line 2209), proof: 'adjoint functors are unique up to unique isomorphism, and Lemma lemma-pushforward-composition'; the composite adjunction is the one implicit there

proof.text: *Step 3 (the unit condition as an equation of morphisms).* Let $\mathcal G$ be a sheaf of sets on $Z$ and $c:L_1\mathcal G\to L_2\mathcal G$ any morphism of sheaves of sets on $X$. By Step 1, $R(c)=g_*f_*(c)$ has components $R(c)_W=c_{f^{-1}g^{-1}W}=c_{(g\circ f)^{-1}W}$. Two morphisms of sheaves of sets $\mathcal G\to RL_2\mathcal G$ are equal if and only if their components agree on every element of $\mathcal G(W)$ for every open $W\subseteq Z$. With the formula of Step 2 for $\eta_1$, the condition of the statement, $c_{(g\circ f)^{-1}W}(\eta^f_{g^{-1}\mathcal G,g^{-1}W}(\eta^g_{\mathcal G,W}(s)))=\eta^{g\circ f}_{\mathcal G,W}(s)$ for all $W$ and $s\in\mathcal G(W)$, is therefore equivalent to the equation $(\ast)$ $R(c)\circ\eta_{1,\mathcal G}=\eta_{2,\mathcal G}$ of morphisms $\mathcal G\to RL_2\mathcal G$.

source.place: Sheaves, Section 008C (section-presheaves-functorial): definition of $f_*$ (Lemma 008D, label lemma-pushforward-sheaf) and of morphisms of sheaves

proof.text: *Step 4 (existence, isomorphism, naturality).* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] to the categories $\mathrm{Sh}(Z)$, $\mathrm{Sh}(X)$, the adjunctions $L_1\dashv R_1:=R$ (unit $\eta_1$) and $L_2\dashv R_2:=R$ (unit $\eta_2$) of Step 2, and $\delta=\mathrm{id}_R:R_2\to R_1$, a natural isomorphism. It gives a natural transformation $c:L_1\to L_2$, i.e. morphisms $c_{\mathcal G}:f^{-1}g^{-1}\mathcal G\to(g\circ f)^{-1}\mathcal G$ natural in $\mathcal G$, with $R(c_{\mathcal G})\circ\eta_{1,\mathcal G}=\eta_{2,\mathcal G}$ for every $\mathcal G$, and $c$ is a natural isomorphism, so every $c_{\mathcal G}$ is an isomorphism of sheaves of sets. By Step 3 each $c_{\mathcal G}$ satisfies the condition of the statement.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma Tag 008I (label lemma-pullback-composition, line 2209), proof: 'adjoint functors are unique up to unique isomorphism'

proof.text: *Step 5 (uniqueness for each $\mathcal G$ separately).* Let $\mathcal G$ be a sheaf of sets on $Z$ and $c':L_1\mathcal G\to L_2\mathcal G$ any morphism satisfying the condition of the statement. By Step 3, $R(c')\circ\eta_{1,\mathcal G}=\eta_{2,\mathcal G}$, and by Step 4 also $R(c_{\mathcal G})\circ\eta_{1,\mathcal G}=\eta_{2,\mathcal G}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-adjunct-counit-identity] to the composite adjunction $L_1\dashv R$ of Step 2 (unit $\eta_1$, counit $\varepsilon_1$, triangle identities by [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]) with $A=\mathcal G$, $B=L_2\mathcal G$ and $\psi=\eta_{2,\mathcal G}$: from $\psi=R(c')\circ\eta_{1,\mathcal G}$ it gives $c'=\varepsilon_{1,B}\circ L_1(\psi)$, and from $\psi=R(c_{\mathcal G})\circ\eta_{1,\mathcal G}$ it gives $c_{\mathcal G}=\varepsilon_{1,B}\circ L_1(\psi)$. Hence $c'=c_{\mathcal G}$: the morphism of the statement exists and is unique for each $\mathcal G$, it is $c_{\mathcal G}$ of Step 4, an isomorphism, and the family $(c_{\mathcal G})_{\mathcal G}$ is natural in $\mathcal G$ by Step 4.
